summary: The exact candidate restores sglang:avg_request_queue_latency as a live Prometheus gauge, computes it from initialized monotonic waiting-queue timestamps, and refreshes it from both prefill and decode reporting. A failing-base/passing-candidate registry probe and independent numerical/exposition cases verify the original metric-availability contract.

tests.what_was_measured: The source-checkout SchedulerMetricsCollector did not register or expose sglang:avg_request_queue_latency; output recorded has_metric: False.
The exact candidate source registered and exposed sglang:avg_request_queue_latency in an isolated Prometheus registry; output recorded has_metric: True.
Candidate regression: 4 tests passed for mean live wait, empty queue, uninitialized timestamps, and future timestamps.
Existing metrics backend compatibility: 33 tests and 4 subtests passed.
Independent boundary calculations and exact Prometheus numeric exposition passed; imported source was /job/repo/python/sglang/__init__.py.

gpu_execution_evidence: No GPU workload was launched by this independent review. rocm-smi identified the assigned idle device as AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950. The candidate's committed single-gfx950 tiny-Llama serving evidence was inspected separately and not generalized to the original TP=8 NVIDIA deployment.
remaining_limitations: No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. The review host has one gfx950 AMD GPU with ROCm 7.2 and no production weights; it cannot reproduce the original eight-GPU NVIDIA TP=8 DP-attention deployment. Full distributed and production-load behavior remains untested, although no architecture-specific code is involved in the corrected metric registration and calculation.
